subject: DataTable not reacting to dynamic input and problem with action button dependency

messages.author: f36f1442a63b65aa
messages.subject: DataTable not reacting to dynamic input and problem with action button dependency
parts:
Hi,

I want to create a shiny app with which users can inspect a dataset depending on a selection of filters. After that, depending on the filters there will be some text processing and finally a plot. A first version of this app is already available here:

http://141.13.250.84:443/pathways

My first problem at the moment is that values for two inputs (party and year) are dependent on an earlier input (country), which selects the corresponding dataset. Every filter for the rendered datatable works perfectly except those two, so I assume this is due to the dynamic creation of these inputs.

The output of the plot is also dependent on the filter selection and because of some computations I want the plot to only show after submitting changes with a button. For some reason, the plot nevertheless update without a button press, which is the second problem I cannot solve.

This is my server.R file:


library(shiny)

source('helper.R')  # loads helper functions and datasets


shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  

    observe({
     
    # select dataset   
    cntry <- input$country
    
    if (cntry  == "UK") {
      df_ <- uk
      lang <- "english"
    }
    
    else if (cntry  == "DE") {
      df_ <- de
      lang <- "german"
    }
    
    else if (cntry  == "FR") {
      df_ <- fr
      lang <- "french"
    }
    
    else if (cntry  == "NL") {
      df_ <- nl
      lang <- "dutch"
    }
    
    #update party and years
    parties <- unique(as.character(df_$party))
    years   <- unique(as.character(str_sub(df_$qdate,1,4)))  
    
    updateSelectInput(session, "party", choices = c('All Parties', parties) )
    updateSelectInput(session, "year", choices = c('All Years', years) )
    
    # filter the dataset
    if (input$cio!=2) {
        df_ <- filter(df_, cio2 == input$cio)
         }
     if (input$party!= "All Parties" ) {
      df_ <- filter(df_, party == input$party)
       }
      if (input$year != "All Years") {
     df_$year <- str_sub(df_$qdate,1,4)
      df_ <- filter(df_,  year == input$year)
       }

     if (input$filter != "") {
       fterms <- filter_terms(input$filter)
      df_$filter_ <- str_detect(df_$text, fterms)
      df_ <- filter(df_,  filter_ == T)
      df_ <- subset(df_, select = -c(filter_) )
          }
  
     # generate datatable
      output$df_ <- renderDataTable(
            df_, options = list(pageLength = 3,searching = FALSE)
             )
   
      # generate plot
      # because of intense computations the plot
      # shallshow after pressing an action button
      
      output$flowerPlot <- renderPlot({
        
        
        plotblume <- eventReactive(input$submit,  {
          
         corpus <- mk_corpus(df_$text, sw=input$swords, lang=lang)
         
         withProgress(message = 'Making plot', value = 0, {
        tdm <- get_tdm(corpus, label_=cntry, nr_words = input$nrwords_)
         })
        plot_blume( tdm , weight=input$fweight) })
        plotblume()
        
      })

    })
  
})



Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks and Cheers,
Carsten

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: DataTable not reacting to dynamic input and problem with action button dependency
parts:
Hi Carsten,

Thanks for including your code with your question. It looks like you have several misconceptions here. You generally never want to:

* Assign an output from inside of an observer (well, not NEVER never, but you certainly don't want to in this case)
* Declare an eventReactive or reactive from inside of a render function

Generally, observe(), observeEvent(), eventReactive, reactive, and assignments to outputs should all be performed at the top level of the server function. I can see what you're trying to do here, but it's based on an incorrect mental model of reactive programming. Fortunately, this is the exact mental model I try to counteract in this talk: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/videos/effective-reactive-programming/ It's two hours, or a little more if you follow along with the materials and do the exercises (which I highly recommend), but it will save you many hours of frustration in the future as you start using Shiny's reactive primitives as they were intended to be used.
